Hypothesis: We hypothesize that a refined therapeutic strategy—which employs dual-targeting, multi-ligand nanoparticles for the precise delivery of high-fidelity CRISPR/Cas9 systems to tumor-associated macrophages in HCC, combined with integrated real-time monitoring of TAM phenotypic markers and adaptive modulation of compensatory signaling pathways—will effectively disrupt TGF-β receptor signaling while concurrently calibrating additional pathways that contribute to TAM polarization (e.g., Wnt/β-catenin and pro-angiogenic signals). This integrated intervention is predicted to induce a robust reprogramming of TAMs from an immunosuppressive M2 phenotype to a pro-inflammatory M1 phenotype, resulting in enhanced antigen presentation, effector T-cell activation, and attenuation of VEGF-mediated angiogenesis. Implementation of inducible safety switches and advanced nanoparticle tracking methods (via digital PCR and live-cell imaging) will ensure precision, minimal off-target effects, and dynamic control over the immune microenvironment, thereby synergizing with and boosting the efficacy of conventional immunotherapies in HCC.
Abstract: In hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), chronic liver injury induces inflammation, setting the stage for an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) characterized by the accumulation of tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) with high TGF-β signaling. We propose a novel, multi-faceted therapeutic strategy that leverages dual-targeting, multi-ligand nanoparticles to deliver high-fidelity CRISPR/Cas9 systems specifically to TAMs. In our refined approach, CRISPR/Cas9-mediated disruption of TGF-β receptor (TGF-βR) signaling is synergistically augmented by real-time monitoring and adaptive regulation of complementary pathways (e.g., Wnt/β-catenin and pro-angiogenic signaling). This dual-action strategy not only reprograms TAMs from an immunosuppressive M2 phenotype to a pro-inflammatory M1 phenotype but also addresses compensatory signals that may limit reprogramming efficacy. Incorporation of inducible safety switches, digital PCR-based nanoparticle tracking and live-cell imaging ensures precise gene editing, robust biodistribution analysis, and dynamic immune modulation. Consequently, enhanced antigen presentation and effector T-cell activation are expected, leading to improved efficacy of conventional immunotherapies in HCC.
CausalChain: Chronic liver injury and inflammation -> Recruitment and polarization of TAMs with high TGF-β signaling -> Establishment of an immunosuppressive TME -> Dual-targeting nanoparticles deliver high-fidelity CRISPR/Cas9 to TAMs, coupled with real-time monitoring of TAM signaling -> Disruption of TGF-βR signaling and adaptive modulation of secondary pathways -> Reprogramming from M2 (immunosuppressive) to M1 (pro-inflammatory) phenotype -> Enhanced antigen presentation and effector T-cell activation, along with reduced pro-angiogenic signaling -> Improved efficacy of conventional immunotherapies in HCC
